profile.headline: Data engineer at Finch, building ingestion and write-back for HR and payroll data | I write Beyond the Traverse on what AI agents need from the data they read and write
profile.summary:
The hard part of data work, in my experience, is keeping records right as they change, and AI agents now write those records faster than anyone can check them. That's the problem I keep coming back to, at work and in what I write.

I'm on the data team at Finch, a unified API for HR and payroll data, where I helped architect the data ingestion and write-back paths: pulling employment data in from payroll and HR providers, and writing changes back out. Before Finch, I built data and machine learning systems across several industries, for companies of all sizes.

I write Beyond the Traverse, about practical AI on real data: what agents need from the data they read and write, why context and metadata layers keep falling short, and what holds up once you run it. Most recently I benchmarked entity matching, expecting Jev to come out about 1,200× cheaper than an LLM, and found GPT-4o-mini tied it at about the same price once I gave it a fair prompt and ran it in batch.

I'd rather show the evidence and the corrections than make a confident call, so expect numbers, named sources, and the occasional result that undoes my own headline.

If you run entity data in production, especially where agents create or merge records, I'd like to compare notes. Subscribe at beyondthetraverse.substack.com or send me a message.

Views are my own.
